issue_context.title: console/inspect output for functions is misleading in Hardened JS
comments:
The way the constructor is replaced is tricky. Accessing the getter would trigger side effects and it's as such impossible to identify the constructor properly. We could explore to improve `getConstructorName()` to detect these as "unknown".

The suggestion for fixing functions is something we can do. The current order was for performance reasons, while it's not a big overhead to get the type of an argument.
Thanks, that matches my understanding. Would it make sense for me to open a PR, or is there some process between here and there?

> Thanks, that matches my understanding. Would it make sense for me to open a PR, or is there some process between here and there?

Go for it!

review_comments: to avoid the future footgun of someone accessing a different property on these objects, or adding an object without specifying these exact two properties
(isn't there a lint rule already that should be requiring this? i added one in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/46083)
I'm not convinced any of those would ever happen, it looks like pure overhead to me, I'll skip this time

I fear this might have a performance impact. Could we benchmark the change to see how it influences average cases?
Is the special casing for only `Object` and `Function` also sufficient? We could theoretically track all built-ins, if we want to do this. But what happens if the prototype is no built-in?

We have to draw the line somewhere, I don't think we can avoid special casing `Object` (otherwise we wrongfully report as null-prototype all objects as soon as the `%Object.prototype%.constructor` property has been replaced with a getter); special casing `Function` is arbitrary, we have to draw the line somewhere, and I don't feel strongly about it. Let's see what the benchmark says

Given that the benchmark CI shows this PR performs better than `main` overall, I suggest we keep `Object` and `Function` for now, and if there's a need for including more built-in prototypes to the list, we can discuss that in follow-up PRs.

I guess the performance would also improve further for other objects with more entries. The overall benefit is definitely there for the average case, so that's a great improvement!

I also agree that we have to draw the line somewhere and I am fine with the approach.
